questions.q: The columns of the rotation matrix R_nb (from body to NED) are:
options: The body axes in NED coordinates
The NED axes in body coordinates
The Euler angles, column by column
questions.explain: The first column is where the vehicle's x axis points in NED.

questions.q: The inverse of a rotation matrix equals:
questions.explain: R is orthogonal: R⁻¹ = Rᵀ. No need to invert it numerically.

options: Are different rotations — composition is not commutative
Are the same only for small angles — and these are small angles
questions.explain: For small angles the difference is second-order; for 90° they are completely different attitudes.

questions.q: Gimbal lock in ZYX Euler angles occurs at:
questions.explain: At θ = ±90° the roll and yaw axes coincide.
Double cover of SO(3): account for the sign when comparing/interpolating.

questions.q: The component order of a quaternion in the ROS geometry_msgs/Quaternion message:
options: Any — set by the order field
questions.explain: ROS — (x, y, z, w); PX4 and ArduPilot — (w, x, y, z).

questions.q: A small gyro attitude update over a step Δt:
options: Euler angles += ω·Δt component-wise, then convert to a quaternion
questions.explain: For a small angle δ the quaternion ≈ (1, δ/2); normalization keeps errors from accumulating.

questions.q: The gravity vector (0, 0, 9.81) in NED, expressed in FLU axes at zero angles, is:
questions.explain: FLU: z is up, gravity points down → negative z.
